scope: Theorem 1.3 (Torus compression) of the manuscript “Filtered products and boundary-preserving compression in complex cobordism” (preprints/Filtered-products-and-boundary-preserving-compression-in-complex-cobordism-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 302 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c47745026b3a083c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let p, n ≥ 1 be integers, put t = 2p+1, and choose L, H as above. Let 0 < a < 1/16, let Y be any compact metrizable space, and let f : Y → C(t, n) be continuous. Suppose there is one continuous complex bundle monomorphism Ef −→ T (f, Zan(t, n)) × CK over the entire locus T (f, Zan(t, n)), for a nonnegative integer K < 2pn. Then for every integer U ≥ 1 there are an integer u ≥ U and a continuous map G : Y u −→ C(t, un) such that at least (a/8)un slots of G(y) lie in ∂[−1, 1]t for every y = (y0, . . . , yu−1). Moreover, for 0 ≤ b < u and 1 ≤ j ≤ n, fj(yb) ∈ ∂[−1, 1]t =⇒ Gb,j(y) = fj(yb).
